subject: multilevel SEM_cluster command instead of two defined levels

messages.author: 9fc030cb4dfec755
messages.subject: multilevel SEM_cluster command instead of two defined levels
parts:
Hey,

In my study, I conducted a factorial survey.

 Each person received 4 vignettes in which my independent variable (y0) was varied. In total I got 3 dependent variables (y1, y2, y3). By within-design, the dependent variables are present four times per person, each with different levels of expression. Thus, there is a multilevel structure. (level 1: dependent & independent varables); level 2: person [ID])

(Firstly I converted the original wide dataset into a long format).

 I calculated a multilevel SEM in lavaan.

With this structure described above I couldn‘t define anything for level 2.

Therefore I defined a single-level-model and considered my multi-level structure via the command: cluster = "ID".

#
library(lavaan)

model<- '

y1 =~ item1 + item2 + item3
y1 ~ y0

y2 =~ item4 + item 5 + item6 + item7 + item8
y2 ~  y0

y3 =~ item9 + item10
y3 ~ y2
y3 ~ y1

y3 ~ y0

y2 ~ y1

'
fit <- sem(model = model, data = "data",  cluster = "ID", estimator="mlr") #robust maximum likelihood (mlr) because data are not multivariate normally distributed
summary(fit)

 

I have no experience with multilevel SEMs yet. Therefore I would like to inquire if my approach is correct.

Otherwise, I am very happy to receive any hints on alternative approaches.

 

Many thanks and best regards

Julia
